visual-headings-without-heading-markup: Text styled to look like a section heading is coded as a plain paragraph or div, so a screen-reader user can't jump between sections or locate them.
data-table-missing-or-suppressed-semanti: A real data table lacks proper header cells (or hides them), so a screen reader reads bare numbers with no row or column labels for a blind user.
layout-table-fabricating-data-semantics: A table used only to position page regions is dressed up with header-cell markup, so a screen reader falsely announces meaningless layout grids as real tabular data.
structural-markup-misused-for-presentati: Real structural tags are used for looks not meaning (a heading just to enlarge text), so a screen reader announces relationships and an outline that don't really exist.
visual-lists-without-list-markup: Content that visually reads as a bulleted, numbered, or definition list isn't coded as the right list type, so a screen reader skips announcing item counts and grouping.
ascii-and-pre-faux-tables-and-columns: A table or columns are faked with spaces and line breaks instead of real markup, so it looks aligned but a screen reader reads across into scrambled gibberish.
emulated-controls-wrong-or-missing-role: A clickable span or div is styled to look like a button but has no real link/button role, so a screen reader won't announce it as clickable.
form-label-and-group-relationships-by-co: A form's labels, instructions, required-marks, and field groups are tied to inputs only by visual placement, so a screen reader can't tell which text governs which field.
special-status-text-conveyed-only-by-sty: Special status is shown only by bold, strike-through, or font change with no markup or words, so 'on sale' or 'deleted' is invisible to a screen-reader user.
